# Functions {.unnumbered}

## Declaration and definition

```c
int  square(int n);          /* declaration: name, what goes in, what comes out */
void bump(int *n);

int main(void) { … }

int  square(int n) { return n * n; }      /* definition: the body */
void bump(int *n)  { *n = *n + 1; }
```

Declare before use, or define above the caller. A declaration ends in `;`, a definition in `}`.

## By value, by address

```
square(5)  = 25        value in, value out
x before bump = 5
bump(&x)
x after  bump = 6      address in, the caller's variable changed
```

| | Write | Parameter |
|---|---|---|
| read a value | `f(x)` | `int n` |
| change the caller's variable | `f(&x)` | `int *n` |
| pass an array | `f(a)` — no `&` | `int a[]` or `int *a` |

A parameter is a local variable holding a **copy**. Assigning to it changes nothing outside.

## return

| | |
|---|---|
| one value only | for more, use pointer parameters |
| `void` | returns nothing; `return;` alone is allowed |
| non-`void` | must return on **every** path |
| `return` inside a loop | leaves the function, not just the loop |

```c
void minMax(int a[], int n, int *lo, int *hi);   /* two answers, no return */
```

## Scope

```c
int g;                       /* global: everywhere below it  */
void f(void){
    static int calls = 0;    /* survives between calls       */
    int fresh = 0;           /* new every call               */
}
```

See [Scope and lifetime](scope.qmd).

## Traps

| | |
|---|---|
| no declaration before the call | the compiler complains about an undeclared function — wording varies |
| falling off the end of a non-`void` function | **undefined behaviour** if the caller uses the value |
| returning `&local` | **undefined** — the storage is gone |
| `int f()` | old style, no checking; write `int f(void)` |
| changing a parameter and expecting the caller to see it | it got a copy |
